page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.Standard.E2.64 is a bare metal server designed for general-purpose enterprise computing. The physical platform contains AMD EPYC 7551 processors providing 64 physical cores and 128 hardware threads clocked at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. With dedicated CPU allocation, the server eliminates multi-tenant virtualization overhead and noisy neighbor interference. System memory totals 512.0 GB of RAM, corresponding to an allocation ratio of 4.0 GB per thread.

The hardware configuration does not bundle local storage drives or discrete GPUs, requiring persistent storage and boot devices to be provisioned via network-attached block volumes. Operating on first-generation AMD EPYC silicon at a 2.0 GHz clock rate, per-core compute speed is modest compared to newer generation processors. However, raw parallel execution capacity is substantial due to the 64 physical cores and 128 execution threads.

From a resource allocation perspective, BM.Standard.E2.64 offers strong cost efficiency for highly parallelized workloads where total throughput and dedicated hardware access take precedence over high single-threaded clock frequencies. The balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio supports memory-stable batch processing, continuous integration pipelines, containerized application clusters, web application tiers, and horizontally distributed data processing.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.Standard.E2.64 is a bare metal general-purpose server powered by dual AMD EPYC 7551 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the platform supplies 64 physical cores and 128 dedicated execution threads operating at a base clock frequency of 2.0 GHz. System memory comprises 512.0 GB of RAM, establishing a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU without hypervisor overhead. The configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, contains no integrated graphical processing units, and includes no onboard local storage, necessitating network-attached block volumes for data persistence and operating system installations. BM.Standard.E2.64 delivers extensive multithreaded capacity across physical silicon, trading peak single-thread execution speed for high parallel hardware density. This makes the bare metal instance suitable for multi-container deployments, enterprise application hosting, batch compute workloads, and distributed web serving.
